summary: Saraju Rath is an Indologist and linguist who held posts at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (1906–1983) worked in Indology, archaeology, and history. He studied under Sivaprasad Bhattacharyya and Jitendra Nath Banerjea, served as Librarian at The Asiatic Society in 1943, and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and linguist. He studied at Presidency College, Chennai, and the University of Calcutta, and under Ugyen Gyatso and Sengchen Lobzang Palden Chöpel. He directed Bhutia Boarding School and served the Bengal government.

Sarat Sarma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Manipur University, attested in 2006, studying under doctoral supervisor S. Shyamkishore Singh and teacher S. Lokendrajit Singh.

Sarath Piyananda Weerasekara works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied for a Sinhala-medium PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under doctoral supervisor Deshapriya Gunasena (attested 2026).

Saroj Kanta Kar is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He held teaching and research roles at GITAM, MS University of Baroda, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, and ICPR, and served as Project Fellow (2007–2010) and Associate Professor (2022) at Utkal University.

Saroja Bhate (b. 1942) is an Indologist and linguist. She was a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1979–2002) and served as Honorary Secretary of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 2003.

Sarva Daman Singh is a scholar of Indology, archaeology, and history who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held a post as Professor of History at the University of Queensland, attested in 1958 and 1987.

Sarvepalli Gopal (1923–2002) was a historian who studied at Madras Christian College, Presidency College, Chennai, the University of Madras (~1940–1944), Mill Hill School, and Balliol College, Oxford (~1945–1951). He held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1971–1983).

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975) was a philosopher and Indologist educated at Madras Christian College. He held professorships at Mysore, Calcutta, and Oxford, and served as Vice-Chancellor of Andhra University (1931–1936) and Banaras Hindu University (1939–1948), and Chancellor of Delhi University.
Saswati Mutsuddy works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed an MA, MPhil, and PhD at the University of Calcutta under Dipak Kumar Barua, and held a post in its Department of Pali in 2001.

Sati Shankar Dutta Pandey is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his master's and PhD at Banaras Hindu University (1981–1990) and founded the Global Synergetic Foundation in 1992, serving as its Chief Functionary.

Satiranjan Sen was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University. He served as a Research Scholar and Junior Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University and founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti.

Satish Chandra (1922–2017) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Allahabad (~1940–1948) and held academic posts at Aligarh Muslim University (~1953–1961) and the University of Rajasthan (~1961–1970).
Satish Chandra Garkoti is an Indologist who earned his PhD from Kumaun University (1988–1992). He served as Concurrent Faculty at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2008.

Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan (1870–1920) was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied under Sarat Chandra Das and earned a PhD from Calcutta University. He was Principal of Sanskrit College and held posts at Krishnagar Government College, Presidency University, and The Asiatic Society.

Satish Kumar Tiwari is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD at the University of Lucknow (2011–2017). He held assistant professor posts at Lucknow, Ganesh Dutt College, Shri Mata Vaishno Devi University, Mahendra Mahila College, and A.P.B. Government PG College.

Satkari Mookerjee (1896–1968) was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Ashutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1951) and became Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1955.
Satkari Mukhopadhyaya is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who served as Coordinator of the Kala Kosa Division at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, attested in 1999 and 2026.
Satkari Sharma Vangiya is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied under traditional teachers Ramachandra Shastri Vyakaranacharya and Ramachandra Sastri (attested 1970).
